title: The Scientist Who Tried to Resurrect the Dead With Electricity
hook: In 1818, a scientist zapped a corpse with 600 volts—and the dead man's eyes opened. What happened next was worse.
why_this_can_go_viral: Blends Frankenstein myth with real, gruesome 19th-century science—perfect for dark curiosity.

title: The Biolab That Bred Mosquitoes That Feed Only on Human Tears
hook: Scientists engineered mosquitoes to seek human tears—but they escaped, and now they can smell you from half a mile away.
why_this_can_go_viral: Body horror meets real genetic modification fear; triggers intense visceral disgust.

title: The Physics Anomaly Where Time Flowed Backward for a Split Second
hook: In a quantum lab, particles briefly moved backward in time—and the data was so disturbing, scientists hid it for years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Time travel is a universal curiosity; 'hidden data' adds conspiracy flavor.

title: The Scientific Fraud Who Fabricated a Miracle HIV Vaccine
hook: A researcher faked data for years, convincing the world he'd cured HIV—while patients secretly died from the placebo group.
why_this_can_go_viral: Outrage at human cost combined with betrayal of trust; high shareability on social media.

title: The Biolab That Bred a Worm That Eats Its Host From the Inside Out
hook: A parasitic worm engineered to digest its host's organs in a specific order—keeping the host alive until the very last bite.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme body horror; the 'specific order' detail triggers morbid fascination.

title: The Lab Catastrophe Where a Particle Accelerator Created a Fireball That Ate Through Steel
hook: A stray beam from a particle accelerator punched a hole through concrete and steel—and nearly hit the operator's head.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visual damage + near-death story; particle accelerators are already awe-inspiring, adding danger makes them terrifying.

title: The Scientific Fraud Who Faked a Perpetual Motion Machine
hook: An inventor fooled investors for a decade with a hidden battery—when exposed, he threatened to kill the journalist who uncovered the trick.
why_this_can_go_viral: Perpetual motion is a classic dream; the violent threat adds real-world stakes.

title: The Chemist Who Created a Liquid That Dissolves Everything Except Diamond
hook: Fluoroantimonic acid is so corrosive it eats through glass, skin, and bone—but a diamond dropped into it survived. Barely.
why_this_can_go_viral: Reverses expectation (diamond is indestructible? Not to this); strong visual potential.

title: The Neuroscientist Who Convinced a Man His Hand Was Not His Own
hook: Using synchronized brushes and delayed touch, a researcher made a subject deny ownership of his own limb—then tried to 'remove' it with a fake saw.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme psychological vulnerability; the 'fake saw' twist turns a classic experiment into horror.

title: The Physics Anomaly Where Gravity Seemed to Reverse in a Lab
hook: A rotating superconductor disk caused a small object to float upward—defying gravity by 5%—and physicists still can't fully explain it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Anti-gravity is a sci-fi dream; '5% defiance' is a small crack in reality that begs explanation.

title: The Lab Catastrophe Where a Chemical Reaction Created a Sound That Broke Eardrums 50 Feet Away
hook: During a synthesis, a scientist accidentally created a shockwave so violent that the noise alone shattered windows—and ruptured the eardrums of everyone in the room.
why_this_can_go_viral: Auditory horror is underused; visceral description of eardrum rupture is unforgettable.

title: The Scientific Fraud Who Faked a Study That Made People Believe in Clairvoyance
hook: A psychologist published 'proof' of psychic powers—it turned out he faked all data, but the myth of 'ESP is real' still fools millions today.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into ongoing belief in the paranormal; 'still fools millions' gives it modern relevance.

title: The Biolab That Bred a Bacteria That Communicates in Code
hook: A synthetic biology team engineered bacteria that flash light in prime number sequences—the pattern was discovered by accident, and no one knows why they do it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Mysterious 'alien intelligence' vibe; primes suggest intent, which is deeply unsettling for microbes.

title: The Forbidden Experiment That Gave a Human a Third Hand
hook: In an attempt to map neural plasticity, surgeons attached a prosthetic limb to a volunteer's torso—and his brain rewired to control it within weeks.
why_this_can_go_viral: Body modification meets neuroscience; 'brain rewired' is a shocking display of neuroplasticity.

title: The Chemist Who Died From a Single Drop of His Own Creation
hook: Dimethylmercury is so toxic that one drop on a latex glove killed a chemist within months—her hair fell out first, then her coordination, then her life.
why_this_can_go_viral: True horror story with a well-known victim (Karen Wetterhahn); 'one drop' emphasizes fragility of safety.
